subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: Should automatic remote skill bin probing for macOS app-backed nodes be deferred/backed off, skipped only for proven co-located app nodes, or disabled by default for app nodes?
rationale: Current code supports macOS app-node `system.which` and `system.run`, so the remaining fix crosses startup timing, co-location semantics, retry policy, and documented remote-node execution compatibility.

options.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
options.body: Keep remote macOS skills supported, but delay the initial app-node probe until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff after failed probes.

options.title: Skip Only Co-located App Nodes
options.body: Avoid probing loopback or same-host app nodes that add no remote skill value, while preserving remote app-node probing for actual remote Macs.

options.title: Disable App-node Probing By Default
options.body: Stop automatic app-node remote skill eligibility unless explicitly enabled, reducing warning noise at the cost of default remote skill support.

recommendation.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
recommendation.body: Keep remote macOS skills supported, but delay the initial app-node probe until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff after failed probes.

likelyOwner.reason: The central remote probe and macOS node policy history points most strongly to steipete for this owner-boundary decision.
